newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain asks France to redouble hunt for ETA leaders.
newsitem.headline: Spain asks France to redouble hunt for ETA leaders.

text.p: Spain asked France on Sunday to redouble efforts to capture the leadership of the Basque separatist group ETA to punish the guerrillas for killing a young politician one week ago.
Spanish Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja made the appeal on the island of Ibiza at the start of a meeting of ministers from both countries aimed at improving cooperation.
"We know the (ETA) leadership is in France," Mayor Oreja told reporters. "Efforts must be increased as much as possible to locate the ETA terrorists in France."
ETA, which has fought for 29 years for an independent state in northern Spain and southern France, has traditionally used southwest France as a base for attacks across the border.
Spain has long said ETA's leaders are in France, too, and feared that Paris was not doing all it could to hunt them down.

But recently, cooperation has improved significantly, and Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar's centre-right government had much praise for the former conservative French government's tough stance against ETA.
The new plea came exactly one week after the death of Basque town councillor Miguel Angel Blanco, 29.
ETA guerrillas kidnapped Blanco on July 10 and shot him in the head after the government refused an ultimatum to transfer all ETA inmates scattered around the country to Basque prisons.
The incident set off the largest demonstrations in memory across Spain as an estimated six million people declared they had had enough of violence.
Mayor Oreja, trying to seize on public sentiment, said this was the moment for a renewed push to locate ETA's leaders in France.
France loudly condemned the killing and pledged to improve cooperation with Spain against ETA.
French Justice Minister Elisabeth Guigou said last week she would expedite the extradition of ETA suspects wanted in Spain. The Spanish government says 36 extradition requests are pending.

"We already have good cooperation," French Interior Minister Jean-Pierre Chevenement told reporters at the start of the two-day meeting in Ibiza. Foreign, defence, agriculture and justice ministers from both countries were also attending.
Mayor Oreja said in a newspaper interview published on Sunday that he expected ETA to strike again soon.
Basque region leaders called on the guerrillas on Saturday to follow the example of the Irish Republican Army and declare a truce, saying the time had come to "put a stop to the killing".
An opinion poll of 800 Basques conducted on Wednesday and Thursday showed that nearly 90 percent wanted Madrid to begin negotiations with ETA if it unconditionally abandoned violence.

Although nationalist sentiment still runs high in the region, a substantial majority of Basques say they approve of a crackdown on the guerrillas and their supporters, according to the poll published in the newspaper El Mundo on Sunday.
